entries.note: He predicts a probable technical necessity, rather than prescribing what ought to be done.

entries.test: Public statements by industry leaders in November 2024 would show whether they treated limits to LLM scaling as established rather than merely debated.
entries.note: The quoted acknowledgment of debate does not itself establish acceptance as self-evident.

entries.test: Public recordings, transcripts, and posts from the weeks before November 23, 2024 would establish which tech leaders used “hitting a wall” and discussed diminishing returns.
entries.note: The normalization weakens the specific assertion that leaders used the quoted phrase into a claim that they discussed the topic.

entries.test: Contemporaneous public responses to Marcus from researchers and executives, compared with the timing of relevant scaling evidence, would establish how widespread and premature the dismissal was.
entries.note: The source concerns attempts to dismiss Marcus personally; the normalization broadens this to dismissal of scaling skepticism generally.

entries.test: Public research timelines, funding decisions, and documented responses to alternative approaches would show whether resistance to scaling criticism delayed research into alternatives.
entries.note: The following paragraph specifies the alleged delay as delayed consideration of alternatives to LLMs.

entries.test: Public investment totals, allocations to alternative approaches, and disclosed investment rationales would establish the scale, concentration, and stated assumptions of AI investment through November 2024.
entries.note: Investment assumptions can be assessed through public corporate statements and investment theses.
The claimed lost progress depends on a counterfactual research trajectory. The alternative outcome is also explicitly hedged with “might.”
